why:
I'm planning a Python script, fibmod.py, that handles around 30,000 large Fibonacci values up to 1e18, estimating roughly 1.8M iterations is fine in Python. I'm now checking whether the Pisano period of 1e9+7 can speed things up, since 5 looks like a non-residue mod that prime, which bounds the period to divide 2(p+1).

I'm reducing the exponent modulo the Pisano period, which takes it down to about 31 bits. Then I'm splitting the index into high and low parts with precomputed tables for each, so every query becomes a constant-time combination.

act.cmd: cd /Users/kethuda/work/razi-cells/exp/s3d2/fibmod; K=/Users/kethuda/Work/razi-cells/kits/public/fibmod; wc -l $K/in-0.txt; time python3 fibmod.py < $K/in-0.txt | cmp - $K/out-0.txt && echo OK; echo 10 | python3 fibmod.py

why:
The body already passes the samples and the baseline is registered, with 72 energy in hand. Further optimization might earn more energy but would cost something. The real worry is correctness on hidden inputs up to 10^18, so I'm checking that the Pisano-period modulus Q = 2(P+1) holds for 1e9+7.

I've confirmed the n=0 edge case and the empty input both come out right, and the recurrence for the h tables checks out against the Fibonacci identities. The samples already pass, so I'm treating the current solution as settled and not chasing marginal gains that would cost energy.
